title: My part in a team
subject: Careers

objective_verbatim: Carry out an agreed role and explain how it helps a team.
display_objective: Do an agreed role. Show how it helps the team.
approved_activity: Choose a role in a fictional team task: sort, count or check classroom materials. Complete the agreed part, pass the work on clearly and review one helpful action.
where_this_leads: This helps me understand responsibility and working with others.

For each team, print Support Cards pages 1–3. Adults cut the five large shape cards on page 2: three circles and two squares. Keep the sorting mat on page 3 whole. Use a separate set for the adult model. Each learner needs both evidence pages. Agree sort, count and check roles before starting; record who does each role. Use teams of two or three. An adult fills any unchosen role. For four learners, use two pairs with adult support. A learner may work with an adult instead of peers. Everyone completes a role; no learner is assessed only as an observer.
Year A · Autumn 2 Week 5: 30 November–4 December 2026. One 40-minute lesson; no day or clock slot is inferred. This lesson is formative. Week 7 is assessing.

A is the useful handover: it states what is done and what the next person needs to do. B leaves the next worker to guess; C takes over their role. If uncertain, show the role cards again and model a handover with a separate set. A clear point to the completed group and next role card can communicate the same message.
Supported: Choose between two role cards with help. Carry out the agreed role, use a handover stem and point or say how it helped. Record each prompt.
Independent: Agree a role, complete it and pass the work on with a clear message. Explain one way the contribution helped the team.
Aspire: Complete the agreed role, then inspect a separate mock set with one square missing. Explain what the next worker needs to know and suggest a clear repair.

Use two minutes to choose and agree roles. Use six minutes for the sort → count → check chain and clear handovers. Use four minutes to review each contribution and, if useful, retry after a specific prompt. The sorter groups the cards by shape; the counter reports each total; the checker compares the work with the task card. Keep the first attempt separate from any repair. An adult can take the other roles.

Use fictional unnamed jobs, employers and settings. Use large paper cards on a clear table; adults prepare cutting. No machinery, lifting or real workplace task is needed. Do not ask about body, family or private experiences. Allow an adult partner, a quiet response, a communication aid or a pause. Learners can query unclear or unsafe instructions. Follow the setting’s usual route if a concern is raised.

For each learner, record the agreed role, their actual action and accuracy, the handover words or gesture, the recipient’s response and the learner’s explanation of how that action helped. Keep prompts and changes separate. A finished team set does not prove every person contributed. Observe each learner’s own role as it happens.

Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // self-edit · ? read back · R responded · E evidence in the evidence record. R requires Voice, Audience, a specific NS+ prompt and the learner response in their own colour. E is recorded only when actual work is banked. Record support and unfinished work. Blank forms and adult models are not learner evidence.

Space: calm seating and clear resources. Voice: choose a response mode, explain a choice or request help. Audience: an adult listens, replies and allows time. Influence: record any change to support or the next task in response.

S: reflect on a contribution, skill or next step. So: listen, hand work on and explain a link to another person. IL: choose a response mode and request a pause or support. MR: allow each person time, acknowledge their contribution and avoid ridicule.
Offer the actual handover and explanation to the Communication portfolio. Record the intended audience, the actual message, the reply and any change. Staff confirm any mapping from the work.

An adult can take the other roles.

Use fictional unnamed jobs, employers and settings. Use large paper cards on a clear table; adults prepare cutting. No machinery, lifting or real workplace task is needed. Do not ask about body, family or private experiences. Allow an adult partner, a quiet response, a communication aid or a pause. Learners can query unclear or unsafe instructions. Follow the setting’s usual route if a concern is raised.

For each learner, record the agreed role, their actual action and accuracy, the handover words or gesture, the recipient’s response and the learner’s explanation of how that action helped. Keep prompts and changes separate. A finished team set does not prove every person contributed. Observe each learner’s own role as it happens.

R requires Voice, Audience, a specific NS+ prompt and the learner response in their own colour. E is recorded only when actual work is banked. Record support and unfinished work. Blank forms and adult models are not learner evidence.

Space: calm seating and clear resources. Voice: choose a response mode, explain a choice or request help. Audience: an adult listens, replies and allows time. Influence: record any change to support or the next task in response.

S: reflect on a contribution, skill or next step. So: listen, hand work on and explain a link to another person. IL: choose a response mode and request a pause or support. MR: allow each person time, acknowledge their contribution and avoid ridicule.
Offer the actual handover and explanation to the Communication portfolio. Record the intended audience, the actual message, the reply and any change. Staff confirm any mapping from the work.

paragraphs: These are teaching guides. Record the learner’s actual response and support. The roles and settings are fictional and unnamed.

The fictional sorter groups three circles and two squares. They say, “The cards are sorted by shape. Please count each group.” The counter counts each group and says, “Three circles and two squares. Please check the task card.” The checker compares both shape and number with the task card. The team needs three circles and two squares, all sorted by shape. Each worker can explain how their part helps the next person.

A is the useful handover: it states what is done and what the next person needs to do. B leaves the next worker to guess; C takes over their role. If uncertain, show the role cards again and model a handover with a separate set. A clear point to the completed group and next role card can communicate the same message.

For each learner, record the agreed role, their actual action and accuracy, the handover words or gesture, the recipient’s response and the learner’s explanation of how that action helped. Keep prompts and changes separate. A finished team set does not prove every person contributed. Observe each learner’s own role as it happens.

Expected result: three circles and two squares in two shape groups. Sorter groups by shape; counter finds 3 and 2; checker compares the set with the task card. For Aspire only, prepare a separate mock set with three circles and one square. It is one square short. Keep the mock task separate from the first team attempt.

A team role is an agreed contribution, not a rank. A fast or loud learner is not automatically the strongest contributor. Copying the adult’s handover does not show an independent explanation. The count alone does not prove the sorting or checking role was completed.

Use fictional unnamed jobs, employers and settings. Use large paper cards on a clear table; adults prepare cutting. No machinery, lifting or real workplace task is needed. Do not ask about body, family or private experiences. Allow an adult partner, a quiet response, a communication aid or a pause. Learners can query unclear or unsafe instructions. Follow the setting’s usual route if a concern is raised.

Use the supplied paper cards by default. If replacing them with safe familiar classroom materials, keep the same roles, counts, sequence and evidence target. Record the substitution and support. Do not change the approved objective. For Week 6, a missing earlier example must stay marked missing; any new task carries its actual date.
